changes_made.explanation: The paper addresses information retrieval/ranking tasks, not natural language generation. While it uses sequence generation techniques, the outputs are constrained permutations of numerical identifiers, not natural language text. Therefore, it does not qualify as an NLG paper.
Since this is not an NLG paper, the metrics used (NDCG@10, MRR@10) are retrieval metrics, not NLG evaluation metrics.
No LLMs were used as judges for evaluation.

overall_notes: This paper is primarily about information retrieval and passage ranking, not natural language generation. While it uses text-to-text models and generates sequences, the outputs are constrained to numerical identifiers in specific orders for ranking purposes, not free-form natural language text. The evaluation metrics are retrieval-focused (NDCG, MRR) rather than NLG-focused (BLEU, ROUGE, etc.).
